newsitem.title: USA: US Air liable for actual damages in crash.
newsitem.headline: US Air liable for actual damages in crash.

text.p: A federal jury Friday found US Airways Group Inc. at fault in a 1994 crash of a DC-9 jet outside Charlotte, N.C., that claimed 37 lives, but ruled against awarding punitive damages.
The jury began deliberating Wednesday evening on whether the airline was liable for the crash of Flight 1016 near Charlotte/Douglas International Airport.
On July 2, 1994, Flight 1016 was downed by a microburst, a strong downdraft of air that can occur in a thunderstorm and is considered especially dangerous during takeoff and landing.
If the jury had decided that the airline was at fault and had awarded punitive damages, it would have been the first U.S. jury to award punitive damages in a commercial aviation case.
It was not immediately clear what financial impact Friday's ruling would have on US Air.

US Air's lead attorney, Mark Dombroff had argued that Flight 1016's pilots were not to blame for the crash. To award punitive damages, the jurors would have had to find that the airline caused the crash deliberately or that it acted recklessly.
In the cases of those who died, jurors also could have awarded punitive damages if they decided the airline was grossly negligent.
